clue.text: Grand old Australian making the most of his prospects?

definitions.text: Grand old Australian making the most of his prospects?

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
taken as written
a digger is informal for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: An elderly Aussie miner works hard at his claim, hoping to strike it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue pictures an old Australian prospector, who literally digs for gold; the figurative sense, someone courting a rich partner, is the 'prospects' pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chasing wealth through a romantic partner is exploiting their prospects, and a prospector literally digs for the metal.

clue.text: Someone delivering a peroration makes us yawn

indicators.note: read as some one, a part of a single run of words, so the letters lie inside delivering a peroration

explanation.surface: A long-winded orator's closing speech bores the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, as one does when tired or bored.

clue.text: Bird carrying away, say, a bit of bacon

annotationWithheld.why: Bird carrying away, say, a bit of bacon (7): LOON round ARD needs 'away, say' to give ARD and no reading supports it
annotationWithheld.clue: Bird carrying away, say, a bit of bacon

clue.text: Fine feathers on the new brood? Cheers!

parts.note: down is the fine soft plumage of young birds
taken as written
a hatch is a brood of newly hatched chicks

explanation.surface: Fluffy plumage on the newly hatched chicks is celebrated with a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast urging everyone to swallow their drink, much like bottoms up.

clue.text: Trojan youth, for example, capsized when crossing an unknown sea

indicators.note: when crossing means the turned letters span the other pieces
capsized, in a down clue, means the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: taken as written
y is an algebraic unknown
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A young Trojan's boat overturns as he sails over uncharted waters.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Ganymede was a beautiful Trojan prince carried off by Zeus to be cupbearer to the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Trojan prince abducted by Zeus to serve as cupbearer on Olympus.

clue.text: Concentrate when last two characters go up to sign on

indicators.text: when last two characters go up
indicators.note: in a down clue, going up moves the final pair of letters to the top of the word

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention, concentrating on what is said

explanation.surface: Focus while the last two people move upstairs to register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' takes the last two letters, EN, of LISTEN to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join up for military service, signing on for it.

clue.text: Small drink for a footballer

explanation.surface: A modest drink ordered for a player after the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-pint of beer is a small drink; a half-back, or half, is a footballer playing between forwards and defenders.

clue.text: Fix a drink to entertain a pilot officer

indicators.note: to entertain means to hold within, so the officer goes inside

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
PO is the abbreviation for pilot officer, an RAF rank

explanation.surface: Someone arranges to buy an airman a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint a time or place is to set or decide on it.

clue.text: Dirty smudge found by member on holy book

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a finger is a member, a limb or part of the body
Mark is one of the Gospels, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A grubby smear is spotted beside a churchgoer's Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A grubby print left by a hand on a surface is a smudge.

clue.text: Plant Pickwick's friend provided for each one at first

indicators.note: at first says the two short pieces come before the friend's name

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
I is the Roman numeral for one
Nathaniel Winkle is one of Mr Pickwick's companions in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A Dickensian gardener plants something supplied to each guest first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb but names the blue-flowered periwinkle (Vinca), a creeping garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The periwinkle is a trailing evergreen shrub with blue or white flowers.

clue.text: Partners each year absorbed in bridge

indicators.note: absorbed in means one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: in the card game bridge, South and North are partners, S and N
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Couples playing cards year after year are engrossed in their bridge game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' sits in the surface as the card game, which also explains the partners, but the definition is a bridge as a structure that spans a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a structure crossing a river or road between supports.

clue.text: Like some babes no longer in danger

definitions.text: Like some babes no longer in danger

parts.words: Like some babes no longer in danger
parts.note: recalls the Babes in the Wood of the old tale, imagined as having escaped from the forest, the idiom for being safe

explanation.surface: Children who have escaped peril.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having come through difficulties, safe at last, alluding to leaving a dangerous forest.

clue.text: Spoils flunkey's retirement

indicators.note: retirement as a drawing back means the word for flunkey is read backwards

parts.note: a tool is someone used by another, a flunkey or stooge

explanation.surface: A servant's leaving present turns out to be stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are goods taken by force or theft, synonymous with plunder.

clue.text: Virile copper in mother's branch of the family

indicators.note: in puts the metal symbol inside the other pieces

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's gives MA'S
a line is a line of descent in a family
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A tough policeman turns up among the relatives on Mum's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile describes manly strength and vigour, the traditional traits of the male sex.

clue.text: Cheer-leader takes fruit to city music-hall

parts.note: hip is the opening of the cheer hip hip hooray
a pod is a seed-case, botanically a fruit
Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A pom-pom girl brings some fruit to a big city theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer-leader' looks like the person but means the start of a cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome was a grand variety theatre, the name taken by many British music halls.

clue.text: Insinuation originally uttered in French during pub function

indicators.note: during places the middle pieces within the pub and function words

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word uttered

parts.note: en is French for in

explanation.surface: A sly remark first made in French at a pub party.
explanation.definitionFit: An insinuation is an indirect, usually derogatory hint, the same as a veiled suggestion.

clue.text: Weaver practising abstinence in a period of prosperity

indicators.note: in places the abstinence letters inside the boom

parts.note: a boom is a time of economic prosperity
TT, teetotal, describes someone abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A textile worker stays off the drink even when times are good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaver' suggests a loom worker, but it is Nick Bottom, the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, whose head is turned into an ass's, carries this name.

clue.text: Young friend reclined on coarse rug during training

indicators.note: during places the inner pieces within the training letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, training in school

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, to recline
a mat is a rough floor covering

explanation.surface: A child's companion lay down on the gym mat in a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's companion in games is a playfellow.

clue.text: Medication required by a royal supporter

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medication
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN, Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family needs some tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is a column holding up a structure, so a supporter in both literal and figurative senses.

clue.text: Generosity with capital letters?

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor's kindness shown in big lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as LARGE S'S, the second sense is big S characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of money or gifts; split as large Ss it also means big letters S.

clue.text: Former athletics official — one with a lot of experience

definitions.text: one with a lot of experience

parts.note: old means former, as in an old boyfriend
a timer is the official who times races at an athletics meeting

explanation.surface: A retired track judge is a seasoned veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran who has been around for many years is called this informally.

clue.text: Instrument identified by scholars across the border

indicators.note: across means the graduates sit on either side of the border

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, one kind of graduate scholar
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, another kind of graduate scholar
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: University graduates spot a musical instrument across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a percussion instrument like a large xylophone.

clue.text: Party chief's sphere of influence

parts.note: a do is a party
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A political leader's area of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory or field over which someone holds sway.

clue.text: Manual for clergyman involved in practical jobs at home

indicators.note: involved in places the clergyman inside the home-improvement letters

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, covers home repair and improvement work
a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar seeks a handbook to help with his home improvement projects.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY (do-it-yourself) is the British term for home repairs and decorating done by the householder.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a book of rules or directions, as in the Puritan Directory for public worship, hence a manual.

clue.text: Gem of a girl loses head to nobleman

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a pearl is a gem, and a gem of a girl is a pearl of one

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman lets her head be turned by an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Earthy material in many a ballad

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
a lay is a ballad or narrative song

explanation.surface: Many an old song speaks of the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a sticky fine-grained soil used for pottery.

clue.text: Accomplished superior

explanation.surface: A talented person of higher rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means finished or completed, as in 'the game is over'; over also means above or higher in rank.

clue.text: Airborne soldier and girl student describing a ghost

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
Norma is a girl's name
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A paratrooper and a young woman learning something tell of a spectral sighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranormal means beyond scientific explanation, which suits spirits and phantoms.

clue.text: The language is the King's English

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina or Edward Rex, a monarch's cipher, so the King's gives ER'S

explanation.surface: Received pronunciation is what the monarch speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes the phrase 'the King's English', meaning correct English.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Inflammatory note appearing in popular church record

indicators.note: appearing in puts the note inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
CE is the Church of England
a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: A provocative remark turns up in a well-liked parish logbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary describes something that stirs up conflict, like a fire-raising device.
